q: How do I check flood risk for a factory site in India?
title: Checking flood risk for a factory site
short: Check four things: whether the site falls in a mapped flood hazard zone on NRSC's Bhuvan atlases, the highest flood level recorded nearby, what future heavy rain projections show, and what the ground tells you on a site visit. Compare your plinth level with the likely flood depth before you buy or build.
audience: MSMEs buying land or answering lender climate risk questions

p: NRSC, part of ISRO, publishes flood hazard atlases for flood-prone states on its Bhuvan portal, built from years of satellite images of inundation. Enter the site coordinates and note whether the plot was flooded in past events and how often. For coastal sites, also check storm surge and cyclone maps.

ul: Find the nearest river gauge in the Central Water Commission flood forecasting network and its danger and highest flood levels.
Ask the state water resources department or municipal body for the highest flood level (HFL) recorded at or near the site.
Note the plot's ground level against the nearest river, nallah or drain, and whether roads around it sit higher and could trap water.
Urban sites often flood from blocked drains during heavy rain, not from rivers, so ask neighbours about waterlogging.

p: The IPCC AR6 Working Group I Interactive Atlas shows projected changes in heavy rainfall, such as the wettest day of the year, for your region under different warming levels. WRI Aqueduct Floods gives modelled riverine and coastal flood depths for return periods such as 1 in 100 years. Both are coarse; use them to rank sites, not to set a plinth level alone.

ul: Plinth below the 1 in 100 year flood depth plus a safety margin, or the plot flooded in recent mapped events: raise the plinth, store stock and electricals above the HFL, add bunds and non-return valves, or look elsewhere.
Plinth clear of both: record the evidence and move on.
Keep screenshots, coordinates, dates and dataset names; lenders and insurers ask for them.

example.title: Illustrative screening of one plot
lines: Modelled 1 in 100 year riverine flood depth at the plot: 0.6 m; safety margin you choose: 0.3 m
Required plinth: 0.6 + 0.3 = 0.9 m above ground; existing plinth 0.4 m, so raise by 0.5 m
Expected yearly loss if unprotected: stock and machines Rs 2 crore x 40% damage x 1% annual chance = Rs 80,000 a year
example.note: Depth, margin and damage share are illustrative. A 1 in 100 year flood has about a 1% chance each year, and about a 26% chance over 30 years.

senseible: Senseible's climate risk page sets out the physical and transition risk questions lenders ask. For the flood screening itself, use the public maps above and keep the screenshots and dates as evidence.
